notes: Both agree that Lethe's functional mechanism as a negative feedback regulator of NF-κB through RelA binding and DNA binding inhibition is well-supported. High overlap (94.1%) with 16 shared claims covering ASO knockdown, overexpression, RelA-RIP, and EMSA experiments.

Strong disagreement on RNA-seq dataset quality. LLM finds the overall dataset robust despite some false positives. Peer reviewers raise significant methodological concerns about read depth sufficiency, lack of read counts/RPKMs, and statistical threshold justification, leading to uncertainty about quantitative claims. 93.3% claim overlap.

LLM expresses uncertainty about age-dependent Lethe downregulation due to limited sample details and correlative nature. Peer reviewers accepted these findings without raising concerns. 62.5% claim overlap on aging-related claims (C25, C85, C86, C87, C121).

Both express uncertainty about chromatin localization claims. LLM notes that data don't distinguish functional pool location and polyadenylated Lethe retains function without chromatin tethering. Peer reviewers question RT-PCR methodology and whether processed functional Lethe (vs primary transcript) is chromatin-associated. 61.5% claim overlap.

Both accept RelA-dependency findings and stimulus-specific regulation patterns. LLM and peer reviewers find the qRT-PCR validation in RelA-/- cells and ChIP data convincing for establishing direct vs indirect regulation. 47.4% claim overlap on RelA-dependency claims.

Both accept stimulus-specific regulation patterns of multiple lncRNAs validated by qRT-PCR. LLM notes functional significance untested but data quality is sound. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns about these differential regulation findings. 45% claim overlap.

Disagreement on characterization of Lethe as 'unique'. LLM supports the selective induction pattern by TNFα/IL-1β and dexamethasone. Peer reviewers explicitly state the 'unique' characterization is over-interpretation, though they don't dispute the actual experimental findings. Low overlap (16.7%) on claims C22, C83, C111.

Both accept dexamethasone induction data (C81, C82). LLM finds multiple orthogonal methods convincing. Peer reviewers accepted experimental findings on anti-inflammatory therapeutic induction despite challenging the 'unique' interpretation elsewhere. 11.1% claim overlap.

Disagreement on temporal dynamics. LLM accepts oscillatory patterns as part of robust dataset. Peer reviewers find 6hr time point pattern 'quite striking' and request explanation for global resetting, indicating uncertainty. Minimal overlap (12.5%) on claims C29, C31 regarding temporal patterns.
LLM identifies failed validation of Gapdh pseudogenes (C40) as unsupported, highlighting potential false positives. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific negative result.

Partial overlap (24.1%) on Lethe characterization claims (C51, C52, C59-C61, C63-C64). Both support the basic characterization and RelA-dependent regulation, though they group these claims differently with other experimental findings.

Minimal overlap (5.3%) on C77 regarding temporal patterns. LLM supports overall Lethe characterization including temporal dynamics. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about the 6hr time point pattern requiring explanation.
